title: Part Two, Chapter 14: The Sentence on the Underworld; the Sun and the Moon

verses.t: "Hear: we shall tell our names, and we shall also tell you the names of our fathers. We are Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque; so we are called. And our fathers are those you killed, who were called Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu. And we are the avengers of the pain and suffering of our fathers, and of all the evils you did them; and so we are to finish you all and kill you, and not one shall escape," it was said to them. And then all those of the underworld fell down weeping: "Have mercy on us, Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque. Truly we sinned greatly against your fathers, of whom you speak, and they are buried in the place of ashes," they said. "Very well," said the boys. "Now hear, all you of the underworld, what we tell you. Since your good fortune is not great, and your gift is not great, your being heads shall be small. Clean blood shall not be yours; only the tiles and griddles and the vines. You shall be mothers only of what grows old; only the children of the straw and the children of the weeds shall belong to you; the enlightened vassals do not belong to you, but shall perish before you. And the wicked and the sinners, the sad and the wretched who sin: enter into them. And let the taking of men not be sudden; and see and attend to this sickness of the blood," it was said to all those of the underworld. And so began their state, lost and dishonoured, and so began their being invoked. And their power was not great in ancient times, but they were enemies and adversaries of men in ancient times; and they were not gods, nor were they called so in ancient times. And so the faces of these enemies, the owls, were the terror of evils; and they were deceivers and inciters of faults and sins, and they were also double-hearted, treacherous and envious, and they were called the oppressors; and they painted their faces and made war. And so they were lost, and their greatness fell, and their empire was no longer great. And this is what Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque did. And this is what that grandmother of ours weeps and laments before those canes they left planted, which sprouted and then dried up when they were burned in the bonfire. And when the canes sprouted again, then that grandmother of theirs burned copal before the canes in memory of her grandsons; and for this their grandmother rejoiced greatly, when the canes sprouted a second time. And then idolatry began, through their grandmother. And then it was called the middle of the house, and the middle of the centre or whirlwind; and it was called chatam uléu, earth made into a bed. And so the middle of the house and of the whirlwind were named by them, because the canes were planted in the middle of the house; and so it was called earth made into a bed, because the canes were set upon this earth made into a platform, where the canes are planted. And for this reason too it was called Cazamha ("canes set up"), because they sprouted again. And then the name was given by them to Xmucane, because Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque left the canes planted in their memory, for their grandmother. And these were our first fathers in ancient times, Hun-hun-ahpu and Vucub-hun-ahpu, who saw the faces of those of the underworld; and the sons spoke again to their fathers, and they defeated those of the underworld.

And this was their reunion with their fathers, by their doing. And Hun-ahpu found them there in the place of ashes; he went and found him there, where the ashes were thrown; and likewise his face, he wanted wings. And he was asked his name, and his mouth and nose and eyes; and first he found his name. And he spoke little, and only the name of Hun-ahpu was spoken to us, his mouth, and only this was said. And so they first exalted the heart of their father, and the place of ashes remained, so that your invoking might be made there. This is what his sons said to him, when they were comforted: "And you shall be the first to be invoked and greeted by all the enlightened sons and vassals, and your name shall not be lost when the light dawns," they said to their fathers, comforting him. "And we are the avengers of your death and of the sufferings they gave you." And such was their leave-taking, now that all those of the underworld were defeated. And then they rose up here to the world, and in an instant they rose up into the sky, and one of them was set there as the sun and the other as the moon, when the sky grew bright. And the four hundred boys whom Sipacua killed also rose up, and these were their companions and were made the stars of the sky.
